dataset.name: WTC 1 V8J cold load-path gate and cut-set audit
dataset.scope: Post-impact 20 C validation of the V8I core network; explicit capacity audit of the missing core-to-office-floor-to-perimeter and hat-truss paths
dataset.warning: V8J does not convert truss-seat capacity into an assumed core-column bridge. It first identifies the disconnected load cut, then compares that demand with published component envelopes. A capacity comparison is not a force-displacement solution or proof that the physical path existed after impact.

official_facts.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: For an 80 psf service gravity load, each seat supporting a paired floor truss carried approximately 16 kip. NIST Table 4-2 gives 20 C interior-seat vertical capacities from 194 to 395 kip.

official_facts.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: NIST Table 4-3 gives 20 C exterior-seat vertical capacities from 94 to 207 kip for the eight Floor 96 details studied.

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: Immediately after impact, the modeled core-load increase was 400 kip at both Floor 98 and Floor 105, so the differential change attributable to the core-to-wall path between those levels was zero. At 80 min, the modeled core load decreased by 6,748 kip at Floor 98 and 6,783 kip at Floor 105.

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: In the Case B hat-truss checks, outrigger E reached DCR 0.97 at 80 min; the listed exterior columns supporting the outriggers remained below DCR 0.67 at 80 min.
official_facts.confidence: high; Table 4-27 and Table 4-28 visually checked

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: All 22 primary-path hat-truss connections listed by NIST were classified safe at 80 min; published demands and yield/ultimate capacities are retained in the V8G component dataset.

official_facts.label: FAIT_ET_RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: NIST reports 38 of 59 north-wall columns, three of 59 south-wall columns, and nine of 47 core columns severed or heavily damaged. It also reports severe north office-floor damage between perimeter Columns 112 and 145 on Floors 94-98. In the global model, the core carried about one percent more load immediately after impact.
official_facts.confidence: high for the reported damage/model result; this does not provide a surviving truss-seat map

official_facts.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: Each tower face had 59 perimeter columns at 40 in spacing. The built-up box section was approximately 14 in square, but plate thickness varied by location.

official_facts.label: FAIT_OFFICIEL_LIMITE
official_facts.fact: Recovered WTC 1 perimeter Column 142 over Floors 97-100 was specified Fy = 60 ksi. This specimen does not establish all perimeter sections or plate thicknesses around Floors 94-99.
official_facts.confidence: high for the specimen; low for generalization

model_hypotheses.inherited_core_network: V8I nearest-four proxy, 47 reconstructed core-column nodes and the cold_upper_envelope cracked-slab case
model_hypotheses.cold_demand: NIST Case B Floor 98 after-impact core load, 34,429 kip
model_hypotheses.cut_set_definition: At the first cold failure, remove every core proxy edge whose beam and membrane branches have both fractured; identify any loaded connected component containing no surviving column support
model_hypotheses.paired_truss_count_full_face: tower width divided by 6.67 ft paired-truss tributary width, rounded to 31
model_hypotheses.north_surviving_pair_proxy: 31 multiplied by 21/59 surviving north-wall columns, rounded to 11; this is a sensitivity proxy, not a seat-by-seat impact map
model_hypotheses.seat_bridge_test: The isolated cut load is divided by each published 20 C exterior-seat capacity. This is a capacity-only screening test and does not assert compatible stiffness, ductility, geometry, or survival of the floor path.
model_hypotheses.hat_truss_cold_rule: No additional cold core unloading is credited because NIST Table 4-22 reports the same +400 kip core-load change at Floors 98 and 105. The hat truss can redistribute wall loads while its net differential core transfer is zero.

gate.required_condition: The post-impact 20 C model must have a mechanically specified, surviving force-displacement path for every loaded component before thermal studies or Blender coupling.
gate.pass_policy: Capacity arithmetic alone cannot pass the gate. The path topology, stiffness, deformation capacity, connection assignment, and impact survival must all be specified from drawings or a declared validated substitute.
